answer: Before an agent can place a bid in an epoch, it must solve a memory-hard puzzle whose challenge is bound to that bid and the agent’s public key; the server verifies the solution cheaply and rejects reused proofs. Labels such as “cedar” and “opal” can separate task domains, while a cipher-derived challenge prevents predictable reuse. Creating many fake identities then requires fresh computation and memory for each, imposing real hardware and energy costs.
